answer: To rename a web link (menu item) in the Wix Editor: Click 'Pages and Menu' on the left side of the Editor. Hover over the relevant menu item and click the More Actions icon. Choose 'Rename' to change the name of the item on your site menu.

First, make sure you clicked Publish after changing the og:image. If the shared image still appears outdated: For Facebook, use the Facebook debugger (click Debug, then 'Scrape Again' for URLs shared before or 'Fetch new information' for new URLs—you may need to click Scrape Again multiple times), as Facebook may take time to process the new information. For LinkedIn, use the LinkedIn Post Inspector (https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/) and enter your URL; note that it can take up to a week for the new image to appear. Also verify your og:image has an aspect ratio of 1.91:1 (width 1.9x the height) to avoid cropping issues.

To see which items customers added to their cart, go to Reports in your site's dashboard and view the Stores section. Use the Most Abandoned Products report to see products visitors placed in a cart but didn't buy, or use the Abandoned Carts Funnel and Abandoned Carts Summary reports to study abandoned and recovered carts in detail (including filters for customer type, product gross value, etc.). To see how items were sold, use the Sales by Product Variant report to see which variants (e.g., size/color) are selling most, the Sales by Product Category report for a breakdown by category, or the Sales by item report in the Sales section for a breakdown of specific items and services sold.

Wix allows each product to have up to 6 product options (e.g., color, size, material). Each of those options can have up to 100 choices, and you can manage a total of up to 1,000 variants per product.

The provided Wix Stores documentation does not describe a specific feature to mark an item as 'low in stock.' The available inventory management options described are: (1) Tracking inventory, where you enter a specific stock quantity number that automatically updates with sales, or (2) manually setting a status of 'In Stock' or 'Out of Stock.' To indicate low availability, you would manually set a low number in the inventory field if tracking inventory, or the documentation does not specify a separate 'low stock' threshold or alert feature.

According to the documentation, images carried over from your desktop site to your mobile site have limited customization options. You can click the image in your mobile editor and use the Settings icon to adjust 'Reset Image Proportions' and 'Image Behaviors' (what happens when the image is clicked or resized), crop the image, or add an animation. However, the retrieved documentation does not specify brightness, contrast, or darkening/lightening adjustments for carried-over images. Full customization options like filters, frames, and design settings (including Fill Color & Opacity) are only available for images added directly from the mobile editor, not for images carried over from desktop.

In the New Automation Builder, you can add personalized content (dynamic values) when editing your automated email template. Go to Automations in your site's dashboard, create or edit an automation with 'Send an email' as the action, click the action to open the panel, then under 'Create an email' choose Edit and add personalized content to the email. These dynamic values (also called variables) display different information to each recipient based on their contact data, such as their name (e.g., 'Hi David'). If you use Wix Forms as your trigger, make sure to select the specific form so the correct personalized content options are available. Note that personalized content does not appear in test emails but will show for actual recipients.

The documentation does not specify exact dollar amounts. For Google Workspace business email, the cost depends on the plan you choose (Business Starter, Business Standard, or Business Plus). For Wix Email Marketing, you select a plan based on the number of emails you plan to send per month and any additional features. Specific pricing is shown when you click Upgrade in your dashboard.

According to the documentation, Wix Stores is designed for selling physical or digital products (including dropshipping items, digital downloads, and gift cards). The documentation lists 'provide services and take bookings' as a separate Wix business solution distinct from the online store, indicating that services are not sold through the Wix Stores product catalog but through other Wix features.

This behavior typically occurs when the image is set as a strip (or column) background and the scaling option is set to 'Tile' (which displays the image in tile formation across the available space, making it appear multiplied) or 'Original Size' (which may cut off parts of the image). To fix this, go to your editor, select the image on the strip, click 'Change Strip Background' (or 'Change Column Background' if it's in a column), click 'Settings', scroll to 'Scaling & Positioning', and under 'How's the image scaled?' select 'Scale to Fill' instead. You can then select a position under 'Where is it positioned?' to choose which part of the image is in focus. Alternatively, you can crop the image to better fit the available space.

Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly version of your site using the content and elements from your desktop Editor, so your site should adapt to smaller screens. If your site is not displaying correctly on mobile, you can adjust the mobile layout by dragging elements to different locations in the mobile Editor, or use the Page Layout Optimizer tool (click Page Layout Optimizer on the left side of the mobile Editor, then click Optimize Now) to automatically optimize the layout for smaller screens. Note: If you are using the latest Editor experience, the Page Layout Optimizer is not available because Wix automatically optimizes your mobile layout. If issues persist on the live site, check that your device and browser are supported (iPhone: iOS 14+; Android: 9.0+; browsers: Chrome or Safari), clear your browser cache and cookies, and ensure you are viewing the site in portrait mode, as Wix sites are only supported on mobile devices in portrait mode. Changing the layout on the mobile site does not affect the desktop site.

Whether more information is required depends on your current account status and what you have already submitted. If your status is 'Accepting Payments', your account setup or verification is not yet complete, and Wix may request further information during the review process—such as a copy of a valid government-issued photo ID and a copy of your bank statement, which must be uploaded to your Wix Payments Dashboard. For a business account specifically, you should also ensure you have provided: personal details matching your photo ID, correct bank account numbers, company name and registration number/tax ID matching registered information, Doing Business As name matching customer statements, a physical address (PO Boxes not accepted) with an address verification document (e.g., utility bill issued within the last 6 months), confirmation that Legal Business Name, Shareholder and VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN match your business bank account, a document proving validity/ownership of the VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN, a Business Description (Business Type and products/services description), and a color copy of your photo ID and bank statement. Verification may take up to 7 business days. If 7 business days have passed and you have confirmed all information is correct and matches your bank account details, contact Wix Customer Care. Note: you have 30 days from the first transaction to complete setup/verification or your account will be suspended.

For gaps at the bottom of a desktop page in the Wix Editor, the documentation covers two related cases. (1) A gap between the page content and the footer can be removed by adjusting the page height: click and drag the Adjust Page Height icon to eliminate the space between the content and the footer (if the page is covered in strips, click and pull the footer down first to access the main page area), or change the page design by selecting a different preset design. (2) A gap below the footer on the live desktop site can occur when the page content is shorter than the current page length; you can resolve it by changing the page background color to match the footer, adding content to make the page longer, resizing the footer to be longer, or checking the Layers panel for hidden elements causing the gap. Note: changes made in the mobile editor are not reflected on the desktop site, so make these adjustments in the desktop editor.

A 403 Forbidden error is an HTTP status code that means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve this error: 1) Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. 2) Clear your browser's cache and cookies. 3) Go to the web address you are trying to view again. If the problem persists, contact Wix support for further assistance.

Check that your dataset is set to the correct mode. According to the documentation, your dataset needs to be in "Read" or "Read & Write" mode to read collection items and apply sort conditions. If your dataset is set to "Write" mode, it cannot read your collection content, so it cannot display the content or apply filters or sorts. Change the dataset mode to "Read" or "Read & Write" in the dataset settings, and ensure your alphabetical sort condition is added to that dataset. Note that dataset sorts override any "Mirror on Site" order from your collection view, so once the dataset is in the correct mode with the sort applied, your dynamic list page should display items alphabetically on the published site.

To update inventory for multiple product variants (selections) at once, go to Store Products in your site's dashboard, select the product with product options, make sure the 'Manage pricing and inventory for variants' toggle is enabled, and click Edit. Then select which variants to update (all variants, variants with specific product options, or specific variants using checkboxes), choose 'Edit Inventory' from the options at the top right, enter the inventory amount, and click Apply.

No supporting context was found for this specific use case.

To add and format text in a Rich Text field in the CMS: Go to CMS in your site's dashboard (or click CMS in your editor, then Your Collections), click the relevant collection, then click the Rich Text field for the relevant item. Enter the text you want to use and choose from the available formatting options at the top of the editor (e.g., Bold, Themes, Alignment, Link). Tip: Click the Expand icon to edit the text in a larger window. Repeat these steps to add content to the Rich Text field for other relevant collection items. The Rich Text editor uses your site's font theme, so update your site's text theme in the Wix Editor or Studio Editor to adjust heading and paragraph styles.

Users can check your calendar on your website by viewing the Google Event Calendar app that you've added to your site. You control what they see by setting the events visibility in the app's settings: go to the Calendars tab and select which calendars are visible to site visitors (showing full details) versus visible but with details hidden (shown as busy). Private events can be hidden entirely or shown with a custom name. Visitors can then view your schedule in the layout you've chosen (monthly, weekly, or agenda view) directly on your site.

To resize an image: Click the image in your Editor, then drag the handles on the edges of the image to the size you want (the image stays at original proportions when using corner handles). To add text to your new section: Click 'Add Elements' on the left side of the Editor, click the Text category, then drag the text element onto the section.

To resolve the company verification error, ensure the Company registration number / business number you enter exactly matches your company's registered information. Then upload a company registration document (such as a Tax ID, EIN, or Registration Number document) that proves the validity and ownership of that specific number. Also confirm that the Legal Business Name and the registration number entered in the form match those associated with your business bank account.

To enable or disable autoplay for a Wix Video player: Go to your editor, click the Wix Video player on your page, click Settings, click the Player tab, then click the 'Autoplay on load' toggle. Enabled means videos play automatically when the page loads; disabled means visitors must click to play. Note: Videos set to autoplay always start on mute due to browser restrictions. The 'Autoplay on load' toggle is not available for strip and slider layouts. For Wix Blog videos used as cover images, go to Settings > Design tab > Video Settings and choose 'Autoplay' from the dropdown. For the Single Video Player, use the 'Autoplays' toggle in the playback options.

If recurring retries are enabled, the system automatically attempts to collect payment from the customer's existing payment method (the same card) every 24 hours during the grace period. You can also manually retry the payment using the same card by going to Subscriptions in your site's dashboard, selecting the subscription in grace period, clicking Collect Payment, then Submit payment, and entering the customer's card details (with their permission).

The docs state that renaming a page in the Pages & Menu panel should automatically update the corresponding site menu item, and renaming the menu item should update the Pages & Menu panel, but they do not address scenarios where this synchronization fails or text will not update.

If you previously verified your site with Google manually, your site is already connected. You don't need to connect your site in your SEO Setup Checklist. If the step is marked as not completed in your checklist, you can ignore it.

To create a duplicate of your site from the dashboard for testing: Go to your site's dashboard, click Home on the left, click the Site Actions icon, then click Duplicate Site. Enter a name for the duplicate site and click Duplicate. Changes made to the copy do not affect your live site. Note that the duplicate will not include store orders and invoices, contacts and members, email campaigns, third-party app settings, Google Operations logs, or Velo secrets stored in your Secrets Manager.

Since you have a Google Workspace Admin account, you can reset the password for your second business Gmail account as an admin. To reset a user's password: 1) Sign in to your Google Admin account. 2) Click Password, then Reset Password. 3) Choose to automatically generate the password or enter a password. (Note: By default, password minimum length is 8 characters.) 4) (Optional) To view the password, click Preview. 5) (Optional) To require the user to change the password at next sign-in, enable the 'Ask for a password change at the next sign-in' toggle. 6) Click Reset. 7) (Optional) To share the password, click 'Click to copy password', then choose to email the password to the user, or click Done. If the user still can't verify their identity, you can also temporarily disable login challenges: sign in to your Google Admin account, click Login Challenge, then 'Turn off for 10 mins', and click Done.

To access and remove the Google Maps element in your footer: 1) Open the Layers panel by clicking the Layers icon at the bottom of your editor, click Footer, find the Google Maps element in the list and click to select it. 2) If the element is behind another element, right-click the element covering it, hover over Overlapping Items, and select the Google Maps element from the list. 3) If your footer is frozen, click the footer, click the Settings icon, and disable the Freeze Footer toggle. Once selected, you can delete the element.

To require customers to sign up before placing orders, restrict access to the Cart Page so only signed-in members can access it. First, ensure the Wix Members Area is added to your site. Then, in your editor, go to Pages & Menu (or Pages), navigate to your Cart Page (under Store Pages, Bookings Pages, or Cart & Thank You depending on your business solution), click the Settings icon (or More Actions > Settings), select the Permissions tab, and click 'Members Only'. You can then choose whether all members can access the page, or limit it to selected members/paying customers (a member role you created or clients who purchased a pricing plan). Note: customers may still complete orders without signing in if they use methods that bypass the Cart Page, such as the Buy Now button on a Product Page.

According to the Google Ads with Wix refund policy, ad credits added to Google Ads with Wix are paid with a monthly subscription or a one-time payment, and these payments are non-refundable. If you pause a campaign, your remaining ad credits remain in your account and you can resume the campaign using only your remaining Google ad credits at any time.

According to the available documentation, it is not possible to restore deleted Wix Stores products through Site History. Additionally, CMS backups do not affect Wix App collections (such as Wix Stores), so deleted products cannot be restored via CMS backups either. The provided documentation does not describe a method to restore deleted products.

Payouts are placed on hold when there is a failed payout or an unresolved verification issue blocking the transfer. To resolve this, click on the specific payout in your Wix Payments dashboard to see the reason for the failure and the instructions provided. Common causes include incorrect bank account details (the bank account holder's name must match the Wix Payments account owner) or the bank account being unable to receive EFT/ACH transfers. Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard, click Manage next to Wix Payments, then Edit Account Details to verify and correct your bank details, and confirm with your bank that the account can receive EFT payments. Once the issue is resolved, the held funds will be included in your next scheduled payout.

To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) with your Wix site, first create a GA4 property in your Google Analytics account using the GA4 Setup Assistant. Then, copy your GA4 measurement ID (found under Web stream details in your Data Streams settings). In your Wix site's dashboard, go to Marketing Integrations, click View under Google Analytics, click the Show More icon in the top right corner, click Edit, and paste your GA4 measurement ID in the pop-up. Make sure there are no extra spaces before the code. Optionally, select the IP Anonymization checkbox to hide visitor IP addresses, then click Save.

Yes. The free domain voucher is not applied at the plan checkout. You first purchase the yearly Premium plan, and the 1-year free domain voucher is then added to your account. You can view it in the Premium Vouchers page in your Wix account and claim it within 2 months of purchasing the plan when you buy a new domain (or transfer a domain to Wix). The voucher is applied automatically during the domain registration/transfer process, not during the site plan purchase.

Since your site is published and not password protected, try these steps from the Wix documentation: 1) Ensure search engines can index your site by going to your SEO Dashboard > Go to SEO Settings and making sure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled. 2) Check individual pages in your Editor to ensure they are not set to prevent search engines from indexing them. 3) Check for 301 redirects in the URL Redirect Manager (SEO Dashboard > Go to URL Redirect Manager) and delete any that exist for the page. 4) Reset your page's canonical tag to default: go to the page's SEO settings > Advanced SEO tab > Additional Tags > More Actions on canonical > Edit > Reset to Default. 5) Check if the page has a 'noindex' robots meta tag. 6) Verify the page is not set to members only (members only pages are excluded from search results by default). 7) Ensure the page has enough content (at least 250-400 words recommended). 8) Add internal links to other pages on your site. 9) Use the Wix SEO Setup Checklist to optimize your site and submit it directly to Google for indexing. 10) If needed, submit your sitemap directly to Google or submit individual page URLs. 11) Use Google's URL Inspection tool or the Wix Site Inspection tool to check the index status of the page. 12) Check Google Search Console for any manual actions against your page. 13) If the page is still not indexed, request indexing via the URL Inspection tool in Google Search Console. Note that it can take time for Google to crawl and index changes.

For a page without a footer, click on the page itself, then click and drag the Adjust Page Height handle located at the bottom of the page to the desired position. Note: This option is only available if you have chosen the 'No Header & Footer' layout for your page. If the handle isn't moving, there may be an element at the bottom of the page preventing the page from getting shorter (you cannot cut off an element). Move or delete the blocking element first; if you can't find it, use the Layers panel to locate it. You can also double-click the Adjust Page Height handle to reset the height.

To change the order of items in your CMS collection and have it apply to your live site, follow these steps from the documentation: 1) Go to CMS in your site's dashboard (or click CMS in your editor, then Your Collections). 2) Click the relevant collection and select the collection view at the top that you want to use. 3) Choose how to sort: either add a sort condition (click Sort > + Add a Sort, select the field and order, then Add Sort) or manually reorder items (make sure Table is selected as the layout type, click the Reorder icon next to an item, and drag it up or down). 4) Click Mirror on Site at the top of the collection and enable the toggle next to 'Mirror item order on the site'. Important notes if the steps did not work: any sorts you have added to datasets will override the order set in your mirrored collection view, so check your dataset sort settings. Also, 'Mirror on Site' cannot be enabled with external collections or Wix Blocks collections. If you delete a collection view that has mirroring enabled, the order on the site reverts back to the order in which items were created.

The segmentation fault (GPF) occurs when the GTK libraries are installed but are not at the required versions. Even though you have the latest versions of the required libraries installed, Installation Manager on AIX requires specific versions of the GTK libraries to function properly. Having newer versions does not satisfy the requirement; the libraries must be at the exact versions specified in the IBM Required gtk libraries for IBM Installation Manager on AIX technote.

To remove the default compressed references (-Xcompressedrefs) from WebSphere Application Server on 64-bit JVMs, set -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument. This removes the use of compressed references and the associated 4GB memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks. However, this will result in a significant increase in Java heap memory requirements (it is not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required), so the Java heap size should be adjusted to a larger value and garbage collection should be monitored and retuned as required.

The issue occurs because the Administrator user (the Domain Admin retrieved via com.presence.connect.wmmcomms.UserManagementServiceImpl.getPortalAdministrator()) exists on the Base Portal but not on the Realm configured to the Virtual Portal, or does not have access to the Virtual Portal. When syndicating to Virtual Portals, this admin user must be visible on both the base and virtual Portals. If the user is not found in the target realm (resulting in MemberNotFoundException for the admin user), the syndication subscription process fails, which can cause the 'Subscribe Now' window to appear blank or corrupted.

For BPM 8.5 (based on WebSphere Application Server v8.5), use the WASServiceHelper.bat utility shipped in the <WAS_HOME>/bin directory to create a Windows service for the Deployment Manager profile. The WASServiceHelper.bat is a front end for WASService.exe. Use a command similar to: WASServiceHelper.bat -add "<ServiceName>" -serverName "dmgr" -profilePath "<DmgrProfilePath>" -logRoot "<DmgrProfilePath>\logs\dmgr" -logFile "<DmgrProfilePath>\logs\dmgr\SystemOut.log" -encodeParams -startType automatic -restart true. This creates a Windows service entry that starts the Dmgr independently of the logged-in user. The actual WASService.exe command used is logged in WASServiceCmd.log in the current directory.

The error indicates that SQL Server's query processor ran out of internal resources while processing a complex query from Case Analyzer's CAPublisher. To resolve this, set the analyzer.db.updateMode parameter to BATCH in the Case Analyzer store database. This changes the JDBC update method from the default CUSTOM_BATCH to BATCH, which IBM experience shows works better and is more stable with Microsoft JDBC drivers for performance-related symptoms. Execute the following query in the Case Analyzer store database: UPDATE X_CAProperties SET PropValue='BATCH' WHERE PropName='analyzer.db.updateMode'

This exception occurs because two output streams cannot be associated with one JSP file. In a JSP, the default output stream is always created when the JSP is translated to a servlet. Attempting to create and associate another output stream (for example, by calling response.getOutputStream() after the JSP has already obtained its default output stream) causes java.lang.IllegalStateException: SRVE0199E: OutputStream already obtained.

The information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21975233. The bulletin covers CVE-2015-7575, the MD5 'SLOTH' vulnerability on TLS 1.2 affecting WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) and IBM Integration Bus (IIB) versions 9.0 and 10.0 on AIX, HP-UX, Linux, Solaris, and Windows. On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references, Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks are stored using 32-bit pointers and must therefore be allocated in the first 4GB of the address space (the low-memory region). Even when the system has plenty of free memory overall, the OS memory allocator may exhaust this low-memory region first. When the JVM later tries to allocate memory for an artifact that must reside in low memory, it fails and throws a Native OutOfMemoryError (NOOM). Additionally, NOOM can occur due to ulimit restrictions on the number of threads/processes per user (nproc), which may manifest as 'Failed to create a thread' in javacores. To address the low-memory shortage, you can use -Xmcrs to reserve more low-memory space at startup, set -Xgc:preferredHeapBase, or reduce the size/usage of Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks. For thread-related NOOM, check and increase the appropriate ulimit settings.

The provided documentation does not explicitly detail the location of the 'maximum string length' setting or a 'More' tab in ACCE. However, to modify property definitions in ACCE, follow these steps: 1. Launch ACCE. 2. Expand the object stores folder and click the object store to open the Object store tab. 3. Expand the Data Design folder and Classes folder, then click the document class to open the Document Class tab. 4. From the Properties tab, open the Property Definitions drop down and select the property definition you want to modify. 5. ACCE will open that property definition in a new Properties tab where you can modify the property definition as required. 6. Go back to the Class Definition tab and click Save.

The clearing event is not received because the EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after it receives the event, causing the event to be dropped before it appears in the EIF logs or OMNIbus. To resolve this, set the connection_mode in the om_tec.config file on the ITM Server (TEMS) to connection_less instead of connection oriented by changing 'ConnectionMode=co' to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF on the ITM using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

IBM Security Bulletin swg21968399 covers CVE-2015-2012: IBM WebSphere MQ stores the MQXR (Telemetry) keystore password in clear text in a world-readable properties file when the MQXR service is configured to use SSL/TLS connections. CVSS Base Score is 2.1 with vector (AV:L/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N). Affected versions are IBM WebSphere MQ 8.0.0.3 and earlier, 7.5.0.5 and earlier, and 7.1.0.6 and earlier. Remediation: install fix pack 8.0.0.4 for MQ 8.0, apply interim fix IT09866 for MQ 7.5, or install fix pack 7.1.0.7 for MQ 7.1. The bulletin was originally published on 01 February 2016.

To disable RC4 ciphers in Tivoli Integrated Portal (TIP):

1. Log into the WebSphere Application Server and navigate to: SSL certificate and key management > SSL configurations > NodeDefaultSSLSettings > Quality of protection (QoP)
2. Select the RC4 ciphers from the "Selected ciphers" list, and then click the "<<Remove" button
3. Click the "Apply" button, and then the "Save (to the master configuration)" link
4. Restart TIP
